column2: A dealer quotes 7.8010 bid and 7.8030 offer in HKD per USD. Which rate applies to a customer selling US dollars?
column7: The dealer buys the dollars, so its bid applies. The offer is the rate for a customer buying dollars.

column2: One euro buys US$1.20 and one US dollar buys HK$7.80. What is the implied HKD price of one euro?
column7: Multiply the USD amount per euro by the HKD amount per USD. The intermediate US dollar units cancel.

column2: At JPY150 per USD and HKD7.50 per USD, how many yen buy one Hong Kong dollar?
column7: Both quotes have the US dollar as their denominator. Dividing 150 by 7.50 gives the number of yen per Hong Kong dollar.

column2: A customer buys and immediately resells EUR10,000 at an unchanged HKD8.40 bid and HKD8.43 offer. What is the spread cost?
column7: The customer pays 8.43 and receives 8.40 per euro. The 0.03 difference costs HK$300 across EUR10,000.

column2: A bank agrees a single currency exchange today for delivery in two business days. Which BIS transaction category applies?
column7: A single outright exchange for delivery within two business days is spot. A near leg would be paired with a reverse exchange.

column2: An importer agrees today to buy US dollars against HK dollars on a specified date in four months. Which instrument locks in the rate?
column7: An outright forward fixes the rate for a future exchange. Buying a dollar put would give a right to sell dollars, the opposite direction to the invoice.

column2: A bank exchanges USD for HKD today and agrees the reverse exchange for next month. What has it arranged?
column6: Spot exchange without a far leg
column7: An FX swap combines two opposite exchanges of the same currencies, with both rates agreed at the outset. An outright forward has one exchange.

column2: Two firms exchange quarterly interest payments, one in yen and the other in US dollars. Which contract fits?
column7: A currency swap can exchange streams of interest in different currencies. A spot deal or outright forward does not create that series of payments.

column2: A six-month outright quote is HKD7.8210 per USD against spot of 7.8060. What adjustment was added to spot?
column7: The forward adjustment is the outright rate minus the spot rate. Subtracting 7.8060 from 7.8210 gives 0.0150.

column2: Spot is USD1.25 per euro and the six-month forward is USD1.275. What is the euro's unannualised forward premium?
column7: The difference is USD0.025 per euro. Dividing by the spot quotation of 1.25 gives 2% for the six-month period.

column2: One pound costs USD1.3000 spot and USD1.2870 forward. How is sterling quoted for future delivery?
column7: The pound buys fewer dollars forward. The decline is 0.0130 divided by 1.3000, or 1%.

column2: Under covered interest parity, spot is HKD7.80 per USD. One-year HKD and USD rates are 4% and 2%. What is the forward, rounded?
column7: Multiply 7.80 by 1.04 and divide by 1.02 to get about 7.95. Inverting the interest factors would price the premium in the wrong direction.

column2: When banks use the strong-side convertibility undertaking, which transaction does the HKMA carry out?
column3: Sells HK dollars for US dollars
column4: Sells US dollars for HK dollars
column5: Borrows HK dollars against Exchange Fund Bills
column6: Lends US dollars against equity collateral
column7: At the strong side the HKMA supplies the Hong Kong dollars demanded by banks. The banks deliver US dollars in return.

column2: Banks sell HK dollars at the weak-side undertaking. What happens to the Aggregate Balance and HKD interest rates, other things equal?
column3: Balance contracts, rates tend to rise
column4: Balance expands, rates tend to rise
column5: Balance contracts, rates tend to fall
column6: Balance expands, rates tend to fall
column7: The HKMA takes HK dollars out of the banking system. Scarcer balances put upward pressure on HKD rates.

column2: A Hong Kong exporter will receive euros in six months. Which position directly locks the HKD value of that receipt?
column5: Buy a call on euros against HKD
column6: Sell a put on euros against HKD
column7: The exporter will have euros to deliver. Selling that amount forward fixes the Hong Kong dollars received on the settlement date.

column2: A treasurer may need euros if a tender succeeds and wants to cap their HKD purchase price. Which contract fits?
column7: A call provides the right to buy euros at the strike, and the buyer can let it lapse if the tender fails. A forward sale would commit the treasurer to deliver euros.

column2: A share put has a strike of HK$44. At expiry the share trades at HK$38. What is the exercise value per share?
column7: The holder can sell at HK$44 when the market pays HK$38. Exercise value is the difference, before any premium.

column2: A call costs HK$1.80 per share and has a HK$25 strike. At which expiry price does the buyer break even before fees?
column7: The gain from buying at the strike must cover the premium. Adding HK$1.80 to HK$25 gives HK$26.80.

column2: A trader buys a put for HK$2 per share. What is their net result per share if it expires unexercised?
column7: The holder lets the right lapse but has paid the premium. The buyer's loss on the option itself is that premium.

column2: A buyer exercises a physically settled call over shares. What must the assigned writer do?
column5: Deliver shares at the spot price
column7: The call holder can buy the shares at the exercise price. The corresponding obligation to deliver belongs to the assigned writer.

column2: Which term lets a stock option holder exercise before the final trading day?
column7: American-style exercise allows an exercise request before expiry under the contract rules. Settlement method addresses what is delivered once exercised.

column2: A treasurer needs the right to buy US dollars, with contractual expiry between two listed dates. Which contract fits?
column7: A call grants a buying right and an OTC dealer can agree a bespoke expiry. Exercising a listed American-style contract early would leave its contractual expiry unchanged.

column2: A pension fund owns equities and sells index futures to reduce market exposure. What role is it taking?
column7: Selling futures can offset losses on existing shares. A speculator would use the contract to take a price view without that offsetting exposure.

column2: An appointed participant posts both bid and offer prices for listed options. Which role does this fulfil?
column7: The two-sided quotes supply opportunities for other participants to trade. Clearing the resulting contracts is a different function.

column2: Two bids rest at the same price in the HKATS central order book. Which ordinarily matches an incoming sale first?
column7: HKATS applies price and then time priority. Equal price leaves entry time as the deciding factor.

column2: After an SEHK stock option trade is matched, which system registers the position for clearing?
column7: HKATS sends the matched trade to DCASS for registration. CCASS handles securities settlement when exercise results in a stock delivery.

column2: Which Hong Kong clearing house handles options on individual shares traded on SEHK?
column7: SEHK Options Clearing House clears listed stock options. HKCC handles derivatives traded on the futures exchange.

column2: A trader is short two Mini-Hang Seng Index futures. The index futures rise 35 points. What is the loss before fees?
column7: Each mini contract changes by HK$10 per point. A short position loses 35 times 10 times two when the futures price rises.

column2: One standard Hang Seng Index future is quoted at 19,600 points. What is its notional value?
column7: The standard HSI futures multiplier is HK$50 per index point. Multiplying the quote by 50 gives the notional amount, which differs from the margin deposit.

column2: What does the long holder receive at expiry on HKEX's physically settled USD/CNH futures?
column7: The short side delivers the US dollars and the long side pays renminbi. A cash-settled contract for differences would not exchange the principal amounts.

column2: HKEX's standard USD/CNH future moves one tick of RMB0.0001 per USD. What is the tick value on US$100,000?
column7: Tick value is the minimum quote movement multiplied by the contract size. Multiplying 0.0001 by 100,000 gives RMB10.

column2: A trader is long the expiring futures contract. Which spread trade rolls that exposure forward?
column7: Rolling closes the position in the expiring month and reopens the original direction in a later month. It changes the delivery month while retaining the exposure.

column2: A borrower misses interest despite a fully functioning payment system. Which risk materialised for its lender?
column7: The failure concerns the borrower's ability or willingness to perform its obligation. A defective payment process would point to a different source of loss.

column2: A bank delivers yen before its counterparty fails to deliver euros. What amount is immediately at risk?
column7: Once one currency has been paid away, the bank may lose the whole principal it delivered. This is FX settlement exposure, not just the cost of replacing the quote.

column2: Which mechanism makes final settlement of one foreign currency conditional on settlement of the other?
column7: Payment versus payment links the two cash legs of an FX transaction. Delivery versus payment links a security to a cash leg.

column2: A hedged airline gains on crude-oil futures but loses more on jet fuel. Which risk explains the mismatch?
column7: The hedge and the actual input do not move in perfect step. That difference can leave a residual loss even when the hedge moves in the intended direction.

column2: An institution can meet withdrawals only by selling a large bond holding well below its quoted price. Which risk describes the price concession?
column7: A holding that moves the market against its seller lacks market depth. The question asks about the cost of selling, rather than the obligation that prompted the sale.

column2: A solvent bank cannot roll overnight borrowing to pay maturing liabilities. Which exposure is most immediate?
column7: The bank lacks funds when payments fall due. Positive net assets alone do not supply the cash required today.

column2: An incorrect batch file books the same customer transfer twice. What caused the loss?
column7: A processing breakdown creates operational risk. No change in borrower quality or asset prices is needed for the duplicate payment.

column2: A lender discovers its guarantee cannot be enforced under the governing law. Which risk concerns the guarantee itself?
column7: A defect in enforceability limits the remedies available to the lender. This is distinct from the separate possibility that the borrower cannot repay.

column2: False reports about a bank's conduct lead customers to move their business. Which risk has crystallised?
column7: Customer behaviour can change in response to damaging publicity even where the report is false. The loss arises through reduced confidence in the bank.

column2: A bank remains committed to an obsolete business model while customer demand shifts. Which HKMA risk category applies?
column7: A poor response to changes in the market can undermine the institution's business choices. Operational risk instead concerns failures in carrying out activities.

column2: An unhedged Hong Kong investor owns yen and measures wealth in HKD. Which change creates a market loss?
column7: The yen position converts into fewer Hong Kong dollars after a yen depreciation. The loss arises from the exchange rate even with the same number of yen.

column2: Several unrelated borrowers depend on one developer for income. What might individual credit limits conceal?
column7: Several customers can depend on one economic source of repayment. Looking only at individual names can hide the combined exposure.

column2: A fund adds a holding with returns imperfectly correlated with its existing assets. Which technique is it using to reduce portfolio risk?
column7: Combining exposures that do not move together can reduce risk at portfolio level. The method does not require any one holding to be risk-free.

column2: A loan has HK$2 million exposure, 3% default probability and 40% loss given default. What is expected credit loss?
column7: Multiply the exposure by default probability and the fraction lost after default. HK$2 million times 0.03 times 0.40 gives HK$24,000.

column2: A dealer quotes a one-day 95% VaR of HK$400,000. Under the model, how often would a larger daily loss be expected?
column6: About one day in one hundred
column7: The 95th percentile leaves roughly 5% of the modelled loss distribution above the threshold. It does not cap the size of such a loss.

column2: Which measure averages losses beyond a specified value-at-risk threshold?
column7: Expected shortfall summarises the severity of losses in the tail beyond the chosen quantile. VaR identifies the boundary of that tail.

column2: Risk staff compare last quarter's daily VaR estimates with losses actually experienced. What exercise is this?
column7: Backtesting evaluates a model's forecasts against outcomes. Stress tests instead examine the effects of assumed adverse conditions.

column2: An analyst raises every point on the yield curve by 1% while holding other inputs fixed. Which test is this?
column7: Changing one risk factor, or closely related inputs, isolates its influence. A multi-factor scenario would also project interaction with other changes.

column2: A bank models property falls, unemployment and funding withdrawals together during a recession. Which method captures their joint impact?
column7: A scenario combines related shocks linked to one plausible situation. Its purpose includes understanding their interactions across the firm.

column2: A bank starts with loss of access to wholesale funding and asks what shocks could cause it. Which test works this way?
column7: Reverse stress testing starts with a specified failure or viability threshold, then identifies plausible circumstances that could bring the institution there.

column2: A dealing desk takes a position in an unfamiliar product. Who owns the initial assessment of that position's risk?
column7: Business units form the first line of defence for risks they take. Independent functions oversee or provide assurance on those controls.

column2: Which function provides third-line assurance on a Hong Kong bank's risk framework?
column7: Internal audit assesses the effectiveness of the framework, including the first and second lines. Risk management and compliance are second-line functions.

column2: A bank sets limits for its trading desks. Which board-approved document defines how much exposure it accepts?
column7: Desk limits implement the bank's overall appetite for risk. The business continuity plan sets out how to operate through a disruption.

column2: A bank's HK$12 million desk limit is 75% used. What additional exposure would take utilisation to 100%?
column7: Current utilisation is HK$9 million. The remaining capacity is the difference between that amount and HK$12 million.

column2: A bank detects an exposure above its approved limit. Who should receive the prompt exception report under HKMA guidance?
column3: Chief risk officer and senior management
column7: The HKMA expects breaches to reach the chief risk officer and senior management promptly so they can act. A periodic audit report serves a different purpose.

column2: A Hong Kong bank adds a material capital guarantee to an existing investment. Which process applies before launch?
column3: Assessment under its new product policy
column4: Reporting under its limit breach policy
column6: Routine review of desk limit usage
column7: The approval policy covers significant changes to existing offerings as well as wholly new ones. A capital guarantee changes the risk the bank assumes.

column2: Which Hong Kong facility gives authorities transaction data to monitor exposures in OTC derivatives?
column7: The repository collects reportable transaction data to improve transparency and support surveillance. An order-matching platform serves a different purpose.

column2: A flood damages a bank branch and interrupts customer payments. Through which channel has the physical climate hazard affected the bank?
column7: A physical event affects operations when it disrupts delivery of the bank's services. Damage to a borrower's premises could instead impair loan repayment.
